nodes.text: The next day. You haven't been able to shake the image of Cassian's face when Hanami collapsed. That look of recognition.
You find him on the roof after classes, sitting alone against the railing.
He's not playing his guitar. He's just staring at the sky, completely still.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Hey.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: What do you want?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Just checking in. You seemed... different yesterday. After Hanami collapsed.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: I'm fine. Go bother someone else.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: I'm not leaving.
A long silence. The wind carries distant sounds from the schoolyard below.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...You're stubborn, you know that?

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: I've been told.
Cassian exhales slowly. He doesn't look at you.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: I had a sister. Younger. Her name was Mei.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Had?

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: She was sick. For a long time. The kind of sick that doesn't get better.
His voice is steady, but his hands are gripping his knees.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: Music was our thing. I'd play guitar, she'd sing. Even when she could barely sit up, she'd hum along.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: She made me promise to keep playing. To play it right. 'No half-measures, Cass.' That's what she'd say.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: She passed two years ago. And yesterday, when Hanami fell... it was like watching it happen all over again.
The weight of his words settles between you like something physical.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: If we're going to play, we play it RIGHT. That's what she would have wanted.

choices.text: That doesn't excuse being harsh to everyone.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: I understand now. Why it matters so much to you. Thank you for telling me.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...Don't go getting sappy on me. I just... needed to say it out loud.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: I'm sorry about your sister. Truly. But Mei wouldn't want you to hurt people in her name.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: You don't get to tell me what she would have wanted.
He stands up abruptly. For a moment you think he's going to leave.

nodes.speaker: Cassian
nodes.text: ...But maybe you're not completely wrong.
Cassian leaves without another word. But something has shifted. The wall between you is thinner now.
On your way out, you pass a classroom with the light still on. Through the window, you see Tiffany hunched over a desk.
She's writing something. Not sheet music. Something else.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Tiffany?

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: Oh! I didn't hear you--
She sweeps the papers into a folder with one quick motion. Her smile snaps back into place, but a second too late.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: Just planning for the festival. You know me, always working!

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: Are you okay? You've been staying late a lot.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: Someone has to. Especially now with Hanami... well. We need to be ready.
Her smile doesn't reach her eyes. The folder is pressed tight against her chest, like a shield.

nodes.speaker: Tiffany
nodes.text: You should head home. It's getting late.

nodes.speaker: MC
nodes.text: ...Yeah. Don't stay too long.
You glance back through the classroom window as you leave. Tiffany has already pulled the papers back out.
Whatever she's hiding, she's holding onto it tight. And the cracks are starting to show.
